lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: A Forge Master. We've been waiting for one. Ironhaven is still standing, but only just. Talk to the people here — see what we're working with.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: How does it look to you? We've held on through bad odds. What this place needs now is a crew willing to push the frontier back.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Good. You know the shape of things now. Speak with Mira — she has an eye for crews that can actually hold their ground out there.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Bram sent you. Verdant Fields isn't far, but it has teeth. Take your crew out there and show me they can hold a line. Come back standing and we'll talk about what comes next.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Back in one piece. Good. There's something we need from Shadow Caves — a cave system further out. Take this Workshop Pass. It will get you in.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Take this Workshop Pass and search Shadow Caves for the Luminous Shard. Bring it back and I'll stabilize the lift to Dragon Peak.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: You found it. With this shard tuned, the peak lift will answer your sigil. Take these supplies and keep climbing.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The cave gate will open for the Workshop Pass. Find the Luminous Shard and watch for old scout caches.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Your bots are carrying real momentum now. The lift to Dragon Peak should answer the sigil I tuned for you.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: Mira's pass should get you into the caves. Once you're inside, keep right at the broken pillars.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: The frontier opens in layers. Keep one eye on your party order and the other on the sky.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: Bram wants the watchtower online? Good. Take these alignment notes back to him. Once the lamps are synced, we can start seeing farther than the gate.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: One of the watchtower crates held an intact Artificer frame. It isn't fit for the line yet, but it can travel with you if you want to bring it online.

lines.speaker: Edda
lines.text: Mira won't let anyone near the lift until the cave shard is secured.

lines.speaker: Edda
lines.text: The mountain lift is humming again. When you're ready, Dragon Peak is waiting.

lines.speaker: Scout
lines.text: I saw a strange cache deeper in. It was tucked beyond the central pillar where the cave forks east.

lines.speaker: Scout
lines.text: That glow in your pack means you found the cache. Head back before the tunnels shift.

lines.speaker: Edda
lines.text: Dragon Peak's reactors are starving. Search the ridge for a Sun Core and we'll relight the old warding pylons.

lines.speaker: Edda
lines.text: Perfect. The Sun Core is stable. Take this reward and keep pushing outward. The whole frontier is starting to wake up.

lines.speaker: Edda
lines.text: The Sun Core should be stashed past the wind-broken ridge on the eastern path.

lines.speaker: Edda
lines.text: You've done more than reopen the lift. The frontier feels alive again.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: That shard stabilized the old forge rails. With a little calibration, I can reopen the workshop line for advanced components.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: Survey cradle's half buried, but not dead. Give me a minute and I'll kick it back online. Tell Nia the drones are hers again.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: If you find old parts in the wild, bring them here and I can rebuild them.

lines.speaker: Nia
lines.text: Travelers leave rumors behind. One says there is a buried vault east of town. Start with the herbalist's walls.

lines.speaker: Nia
lines.text: So the rumor was true. Good crews always test the hidden seams of a place.

lines.speaker: Nia
lines.text: Now that the peak relays are live again, I can chart farther routes. Toma just needs someone to kick the old survey drone cradle back awake.

lines.speaker: Nia
lines.text: Perfect. The survey drones are airborne again, which means safer routes, better supply calls, and one less blind frontier.

lines.speaker: Nia
lines.text: Travelers leave rumors behind. Keep listening.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Rest when you can. Even machines need a rhythm.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: With the lift alive again, we can finally power the old watchtower. Tor still has the alignment notes if you're willing to carry them over.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: That's the last of it. The watchtower lamps are online again, and Ironhaven won't feel quite so small tonight.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: Hidden chests react to careful eyes. Walk close and watch the outline flicker. And if you find an intact medic frame, I'll patch it into your crew.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: There. The support frame is stable again. It will follow your commands from here on out.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: Hidden chests react to careful eyes. Walk close and watch the outline flicker.

lines.speaker: Ranger Pell
lines.text: The roots around the Moonlit Glade shift every dusk. If you can map the pattern with a scan frame, we might finally reclaim the clearing.

lines.speaker: Ranger Pell
lines.text: Follow the roots that hum back at your scanner. The glade should open if the pattern is traced cleanly.

lines.speaker: Ranger Pell
lines.text: So the glade was real after all. Good. One less forgotten place sealed off by fear and old growth.

lines.speaker: Ranger Pell
lines.text: Whispering Forest keeps its paths for crews that pay attention.

lines.speaker: Jora
lines.text: The quarry's jammed sluice is blocking a maintenance lane full of salvage. If your heavy frame can wrench it loose, the whole lift route gets easier to trust.

lines.speaker: Jora
lines.text: The sluice sits just past the crusher line. You'll need a real vanguard shove to break it free.

lines.speaker: Jora
lines.text: There it is. Air moving through the lane again. That's what progress sounds like in a quarry.

lines.speaker: Jora
lines.text: Every cleared machine lane becomes a road for the people after us.

lines.speaker: Captain Maren
lines.text: The drowned archive below still carries intact charts. Bring me whatever route key survived down there and I can point you toward the old command skies.

lines.speaker: Captain Maren
lines.text: Search the Archive Hull. The chart capsule should be sealed against pressure and corrosion.

lines.speaker: Captain Maren
lines.text: Perfect. This Archive Chart points to an air route the old world used to reach the fortress above the clouds. Take it. The sky path is yours now.

lines.speaker: Captain Maren
lines.text: The sea keeps memories longer than the frontier does.

lines.speaker: Commander Rex
lines.text: The fortress rails still answer a proper command token. If the sanctum below the clouds still holds one, recover it and we'll reopen the deepest routes.

lines.speaker: Commander Rex
lines.text: Clockwork Sanctum should still be preserving command hardware. Search the resonance vaults.

lines.speaker: Commander Rex
lines.text: That's it. With the Command Sigil back online, the fortress no longer feels like a dead shell. The final rails are opening.

lines.speaker: Commander Rex
lines.text: The old command lattice was built for war, but we'll use it to rebuild routes instead.

lines.speaker: Clockmaker Echo
lines.text: A final key remains outside the machine's own logic. Search the Abyssal Rift. Only the Void Key can separate memory from collapse.

lines.speaker: Clockmaker Echo
lines.text: At the edge of the rift, the world forgets its own shape. That is where the key was hidden.

lines.speaker: Clockmaker Echo
lines.text: The Void Key has returned to the world of form. The final conduit is stable enough for a Forge Master to pass.

lines.speaker: Clockmaker Echo
lines.text: Time is only another machine until it breaks.

lines.speaker: The Watcher
lines.text: You have the key, the route, and the will. Step into the final silence. Memory Lane waits, and beyond it, Origin.

lines.speaker: The Watcher
lines.text: Every repaired road ends where memory begins.

lines.speaker: Nia
lines.text: The herbalist swears there's a sealed cache behind those resin-thorns east of town. Burn through them cleanly and we'll see what the old frontier hid there.

lines.speaker: Nia
lines.text: Don't hack at the brambles. Heat the resin, let it peel back, and the cache should sit just beyond the wall.

lines.speaker: Nia
lines.text: Perfect. The old cache was real, and now we've got one more secret route back under our control.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: There's an old trailhead past the southern hedge, but a collapsed boulder sealed it months ago. If one of your heavy frames can shift it, we get another safe line out of Ironhaven.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: The boulder is packed into the trail deeper than it looks. Hit it with pure leverage, not finesse.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: That does it. One more route open, one less blind corner around town. That's how a frontier starts feeling like a home again.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: There's a shimmer wall deeper in the cave that answers every scanner pulse differently. Trace the seam for me and we may finally map the hollow behind it.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Watch for the wall to flicker back in rhythm with your scan lattice. That's where the seam opens.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: A hidden passage and a clean scan trace. That's the kind of map work that keeps crews alive down here.

lines.speaker: Reno
lines.text: The shallows are lying to me. There's a hidden current threading between the rocks, but I need a scan frame to chart it without losing a whole salvage skiff.

lines.speaker: Reno
lines.text: Follow the drift where the foam cuts sideways. If the scanner holds, the tidepool should open on the far shelf.

lines.speaker: Reno
lines.text: That's the line. With that tidepool route mapped, we can pull salvage without feeding another barge to the surf.

lines.speaker: Professor Lio
lines.text: These crystal harmonics are close to Dragon Peak's warding frequencies, but not close enough. Take my notes to Edda and ask how the pylons stayed stable at altitude.

lines.speaker: Professor Lio
lines.text: Edda will know which harmonics to trim. The mountain learned stability the hard way.

lines.speaker: Edda
lines.text: Lio's close. Tell him to damp the third harmonic, then bias the core toward the colder crystal lines. That should keep the vault from singing itself apart.

lines.speaker: Professor Lio
lines.text: Of course. Edda trimmed the instability exactly where I feared it. With this, the depths become a laboratory again instead of a warning.

lines.speaker: Sister Vale
lines.text: The cloister's prayer circuit was really a machine lattice. If the Clockmaker Echo still remembers its pattern, we may be able to wake the vale without breaking it.

lines.speaker: Clockmaker Echo
lines.text: The cloister ran on a closed winter loop. Tell the pilgrim to restart it slowly, one ring at a time, and let the frost keep the timing honest.

lines.speaker: Sister Vale
lines.text: Then the old circuit still has purpose. Good. Even frozen places deserve a pulse strong enough to answer winter.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: Scorched Plateau can teach us a lot, but Volcanic Core can melt a machine that learns the lesson wrong. Take my heat-tolerance specs to Kira and bring back something we can actually build around.

lines.speaker: Forgehand Kira
lines.text: Tell Toma the plateau alloys are overhard. Temper them twice, quench them in slagwater, and they'll survive the core without shattering.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: That's the accord, then. Plateau grit, core heat, and a process that won't kill the crew trying it. That's real progress.

lines.speaker: Commander Rex
lines.text: The command rails are awake, but they still carry ghost traffic from the old war lattice. Ask the Clockmaker Echo how to quiet the echoes before they fry another control hub.

lines.speaker: Clockmaker Echo
lines.text: Tell Rex to pulse the rails in threes, then cut the fourth beat short. The old command ghosts will chase the missing rhythm and collapse.

lines.speaker: Commander Rex
lines.text: Good. That's the rail lattice settled without tearing half the fortress apart. We can finally use these lines like builders instead of grave robbers.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: The pylons are back online. That means the routes beyond Dragon Peak are no longer completely blind. Push out into the midlands and tell me what's actually out there.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: So the midlands are alive — and hostile in ways we didn't expect. Good to know before we send supply runs through. Nia's been picking up something strange from the deep water zones. You should hear it from her directly.

lines.speaker: Nia
lines.text: The survey drones caught a pulse from the deep water zones — rhythmic, not natural. Something down there is still running. Head to the Coastal Shallows and trace it closer to the source.

lines.speaker: Nia
lines.text: The pulse originates somewhere below the shallows. Your scanner should pick up the signal variance once you're in range of the deep shelf.

lines.speaker: Captain Maren
lines.text: A pulse from the deep shelf? I know what that is. There's a drowned archive below — I mapped the approach once, years ago. The signal means it's still intact. We need what's inside.

lines.speaker: Bolt Simulation
lines.text: Welcome back, challenger. Every ten floors, the dungeon will answer with a stronger test. Every return trip is a new proof of mastery.

lines.speaker: Master Silas
lines.text: The forge speaks through its failures as much as its successes. Bring me salvage and I'll show you what I mean.

lines.speaker: Master Silas
lines.text: The basic rails are humming again. With a little more investment, I can retool the alloy chambers for advanced component work.

lines.speaker: Master Silas
lines.text: The alloy work gave me an idea. That old fusion cradle in the back — it can be restored. Fusion work is art, not just engineering.

lines.speaker: Master Silas
lines.text: The fusion cradle is running. Bring two compatible frames to the forge and let the machine decide what they become together.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: A repaired machine still needs care between battles. Stop by when your team looks worn.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: With the base stock restocked, I can start building proper field kits. More potions, better recovery. Your team will feel the difference mid-battle.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: The frontier zones carry materials I've never been able to study before. Let me run experiments. The compounds could change how your team fights entirely.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: The compound lab is stable. Some of these formulas are older than Ironhaven — I'm still learning what they were designed to cure.

lines.speaker: Commander Rex
lines.text: Ironhaven's walls hold because people chose to stay and fight for them. Don't let that count for nothing out there.

lines.speaker: Commander Rex
lines.text: The watchtower sees farther now, but the relay range still ends at the ridgeline. Let me route the expansion and we'll have eyes on every major approach.

lines.speaker: Commander Rex
lines.text: With relay coverage in place, we're ready for a proper command hub. Coordination, rapid response, tactical routing — Ironhaven becomes more than a waypoint.

lines.speaker: Commander Rex
lines.text: The hub is operational. Every field unit we send out now has a real command structure behind it. That changes what's possible.

lines.speaker: Professor Cogs
lines.text: Every battle logged is data. Every rout survived is a dissertation. Keep fighting and I'll keep learning.

lines.speaker: Professor Cogs
lines.text: The drones are feeding us raw survey data, but without proper vaults to index it we're drowning in noise. Fund the data vaults and I'll turn noise into knowledge.

lines.speaker: Professor Cogs
lines.text: The vaults gave me the patterns I needed. There is a design space in the data that no standard forging method reaches. Give me a prototype lab and I'll show you what the frontier was actually trying to build.

lines.speaker: Professor Cogs
lines.text: The prototype lab is running. What I'm seeing in the foundry data could rewrite everything we thought we knew about pre-collapse engineering.

lines.speaker: Bolt
lines.text: A Forge Master with your record? I've been waiting for you to swing by. The dungeon's calling if you're ready for a real test.

lines.speaker: Bolt
lines.text: Now that the command hub is online, I can track your dungeon runs properly. Every ten floors, expect the parameters to shift. I'll be watching.

lines.speaker: Jax
lines.text: If it's broken, lost, or forgotten, I probably know where it ended up. And if I don't, I'll find out for the right price.

lines.speaker: Jax
lines.text: There's a sealed supply cache in the quarry's lower lane — old enough that even Jora doesn't know what's in it. Help me crack it open and we split whatever's inside.

lines.speaker: Jax
lines.text: Quarry lower lane, past the sluice. The cache has a triple-lock seal — your scanner can read the combination off the corrosion pattern.

lines.speaker: Jax
lines.text: Pre-collapse salvage, barely touched by the weather. That's a solid find, partner. Consider this the start of something good.

lines.speaker: Kira
lines.text: The forge doesn't care about rank. It only cares about heat and patience. I've got plenty of both.

lines.speaker: Kira
lines.text: After the plateau accord, I finally had enough material to set up a proper Ironhaven smithy. If Master Silas needs heat work done right, he knows where I am.
